key_insight: Combining Koopman-structured linear dynamics with probabilistic learning produces accurate forecasts with calibrated uncertainty in several nonlinear-system experiments.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a potentially lower-cost alternative to deep ensembles for uncertainty-aware forecasting in applications such as fluid dynamics.
method: Learn observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators using machine learning architectures.
Push injected noise samples through the model to generate predictive ensembles.
Train with the continuous ranked probability score to target accurate, calibrated forecasts.
evidence_signal: Tests on two nonlinear ODE systems, vortex shedding, and cavity flow showed spread–skill ratios near one in several experiments and low-noise forecast accuracy extending to 2–20 times the training horizon.
watch_item: Calibration can degrade during extended rollouts or with noisy data, producing under- or over-dispersed ensembles.
paper_title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
